# Bitfroest.fs 0.0.50

Changes since the published version [0.0.49](https://github.com/s-a/Bitfroest.fs/releases/tag/v0.0.49).

## 🚀 Linux support: closer to full coverage

Linux x64 support now includes native file operations and desktop clipboard integration, with more work ahead toward full Linux coverage. Remaining limits include symbolic-link extended attributes, Wayland sessions without supported clipboard access, and filesystem or permission restrictions. Details are listed under **Known limitations** below.

Community testing, contributions and feedback are welcome and appreciated. Problems can be reported in [GitHub issues](https://github.com/s-a/Bitfroest.fs/issues). Reports are most useful with the Linux distribution and version, desktop environment, X11 or Wayland session type, and steps to reproduce.

## Added

- Native Linux file copying with measured progress, cancellation and destination identity checks.
- Linux symbolic-link copying, moving, renaming and deletion preserve the link object and its target text. Explicit navigation resolves permitted directory links to their canonical target.
- Linux system file clipboard support through X11, Wayland data control and existing XWayland connections. Private compositor integration tests cover GNOME/Mutter and KDE/KWin.
- Native Linux Git index transactions with guarded publication and cancellation.

## Improved

- Linux copying preserves file and directory permissions, ownership, timestamps, extended attributes and POSIX ACLs when permitted by the filesystem and current access rights. Sparse copying retains reported holes and separates logical progress from bytes written.
- Copy publication on Linux uses an exclusive rename and works on filesystems without hardlink support, including the tested FAT fixture.
- The README includes an ordered screenshot and animation gallery with shortcuts, gestures, native editor examples and real folder-lock inspection with unconfirmed action previews.
- The current-directory symbol can be selected for name and path commands. Its context actions operate on the current folder. Filesystem roots omit the parent-directory row.

## Fixed

- Wayland clipboard cleanup releases only the extension's own source and preserves a competing selection that replaces it.
- Partial move acknowledgement updates the owned clipboard source without replacing a competing selection. Previously cached clipboard data cannot be forcibly refreshed in other applications.
- Cancelling a Linux folder move preserves empty destination subfolders and retains source directories whose metadata has not been confirmed at the destination.
- Clipboard connection failures settle pending requests and allow a subsequent explicit operation to establish a new session.
- Linux copy and native Git progress callbacks finish before their operation promises complete. Cancellation and shutdown release pending callback resources.
- Linux native file workers reject FIFO replacements without blocking on a file open. Copy and Git operations release rejected descriptors and preserve foreign destination replacements.
- ZIP operation progress uses phase totals for its overall measurement.

## Known limitations

- Packages target Windows x64 and Linux x64. Linux requires Ubuntu 24.04 or a compatible newer runtime; macOS is not officially supported.
- Linux cannot reproduce the Windows shell context menu. Native icons depend on installed GIO, GdkPixbuf and image loaders.
- System clipboard access requires a supported desktop protocol and permission. Compositors offering neither permitted data control nor XWayland remain unavailable. A named Wayland display is required; raw inherited `WAYLAND_SOCKET` connections are not shared. Clipboard persistence after the native session closes is not guaranteed.
- Filesystems and access rights can prevent metadata preservation. Symbolic-link extended attributes cannot currently be copied through the required stable identity-based API and produce an explicit unsupported-metadata error.
- Blocking filesystem calls can only observe cooperative cancellation after the operating system returns. Specialized split or sparse Git index layouts and external Git filters remain outside the supported transaction contract.
- Headless integration tests do not establish visual acceptance for every Linux desktop, distribution or compositor version.
